item.title: 'God made Trump': Inside White House's $20 million ad campaign ahead of midterms
item.description: Three of the advertisements have so far appeared on television networks including CBS, CNN, MS NOW, Fox News and Fox. It remains unclear whether every advertisement will be broadcast on television, released digitally or both. Although the videos have different themes, many feature Trump alongside audio containing favourable comments about him from news reports.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Security lapse Israel overlooked? Over 12 Omani pilots flew to Tel Aviv despite ban
item.description: Israeli passengers, the captain and other pilots on board intervened, allowing the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were Israeli and were later flown from Saudi Arabia to Israel. Oman does not have diplomatic relations with Israel. According to the report, rules introduced after 2020 Abraham Accords prohibit pilots from countries that do not have relations with Israel from flying into the country.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Women in Munich Oktoberfest given free shorts to prevent upskirting
item.description: At least 32,000 videos featuring women on the Teufelsrad have been circulated, according to Munich daily Süddeutsche Zeitung. Some have apparently been watched millions of times. The videos often show women wearing traditional dirndl dresses with their underwear visible. Some images have also been digitally manipulated to make the women appear naked, according to BR.

item.title: Hindu temple hit with bricks in US; Hindu groups demand swift action
item.description: An attack on the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights occurred while devotees were present. The incident involved bricks being thrown at the temple, resulting in shattered windows. Surveillance footage is being reviewed by authorities to identify the perpetrator. This potential hate crime coincides with Hindu Heritage Month and upcoming Navratri celebrations.
item.dc:creator: Kanchan Yadav

item.title: Streamer Details Alleged Abuse: Lyndi alleges domestic and sexual assault; denies blackmailing RatedEpicz
item.description: Twitch streamer Lindsay “Lyndi” has opened up about what she says was domestic and sexual abuse during a past relationship with Neil “RatedEpicz”. She also denied blackmail claims and said she accepts responsibility for her own hurtful actions. Lyndi said she shared her story after the Cornell sexual assault case brought back painful memories and encouraged others to speak up.

item.title: An Oregon farming couple had 13 wind turbines placed on their land; while crops continued around them
item.description: In Sherman County, Oregon, a wheat-farming family thrives, thanks to the wind turbines dotting their property. These turbines not only allow for uninterrupted traditional farming practices but also generate crucial income through payments from renewable energy projects. The McCullough family's success story highlights a unique blend of agriculture and sustainable energy, benefiting not just them but also providing significant tax revenue that nurtures local services and supports rural infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Elizabeth Mata bought 94 acres in North Carolina in 1973; an I-540 corridor later restricted 9.93 acres
item.description: In a landmark decision, the North Carolina Supreme Court has resolved a crucial land dispute involving landowner Elizabeth Mata. The court ruled that the state’s long-standing restrictions on her property, stemming from a proposed highway project, constituted indefinite takings. This ruling mandates proper compensation under eminent domain principles. The determination of the exact compensation will now be delegated back to trial courts, marking an essential step in the legal proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Did Elon Musk and Shivon Zilis break up? 'It's hard to go from in love to let go in a week with no warning'
item.description: Elon Musk-Shivon Zilis breakup: Shivon showed her September 24 conversation with Elon where Elon told her that he did not realize that the dinner with Xi included "significant other," or he would have invited her. The breakup happened in one week, Shivon said, adding that there was no warning and that she was hurting.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: London sent 3 million tonnes of railway soil to rebuild Essex wetlands; bird numbers hit 39,000
item.description: More than three million tonnes of soil excavated for London’s Elizabeth line were transported to Wallasea Island in Essex to help create coastal wetlands. Ten years after seawalls were breached, the restored RSPB reserve has recorded a record 39,000 wintering birds, including thousands of Knot, Avocets, Grey Plovers and Bar-tailed Godwits.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: A 558-acre Wyoming ranch sat unsold for 14 months; auction plan drew a buyer before bidding began
item.description: A 558-acre Wyoming ranch sat unsold for 14 months despite a price cut from nearly $20 million to $15 million. When the owner planned a no-reserve auction, about 40 prospective bidders visited the property in 36 days, prompting one buyer to make an offer before the auction began.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: In 2022, loggers cut 1,299 trees on Mississippi couple's land; tally helped secure $41,920 award
item.description: In a significant logging error, 1,299 trees were cut down on Gerald and Rhonda Smith's property in Mississippi. The Smiths meticulously recorded the extent of their loss through photographs and measurements, leading to legal proceedings. A court recognized the logging company's blatant negligence, awarding the couple $41,920. Expert surveyor J.T. Strickland confirmed the boundary lines, and the appeals court reaffirmed the lower court’s ruling, validating the Smiths' claims for damages.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 1840s Brooklyn townhouse bought for $5.35M now asks $12.75M after a full restoration
item.description: A restored 1840s Brooklyn Heights townhouse that sold for $5.35 million in 2023 is now listed for $12.75 million. The five-level, 6,000-sq-ft home retains its 1848 Greek Revival character while its electrical, plumbing, HVAC and other systems have been rebuilt.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: A Maryland homeowner received an unsolicited $234,368.25 check tied to an offer for her property
item.description: Effective October 1, Maryland introduced legislation banning unsolicited checks sent with home purchase offers. This initiative is designed to safeguard homeowners from misleading marketing strategies from property investors. Consumer advocates highlighted the risk of vulnerable owners being tricked into agreements upon receiving such checks. Historical precedents in consumer lending underline the necessity for legal protections, advising homeowners against accepting random financial items received through mail.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida approves $72.6M to protect 10,770 acres, including wildlife and farmland
item.description: An ambitious architectural project reminiscent of the Taj Mahal awaits a new owner in Ocean Springs, Mississippi. Once priced at $2 million in 2016, the unfinished mansion is now listed for $2.5 million. Encompassing 4,402 square feet, the estate is a blank canvas requiring extensive renovations. With building permits acquired back in 2008, progress has halted. The current seller hopes a visionary buyer can finally realize this home's potential.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
